title: Λύκος καὶ ἀρνίον ⟨εἰς ἱερὸν καταφυγόν⟩
titleEn: The Wolf and the Lamb that Took Refuge in a Temple
part: The Wolf and the Lamb that Took Refuge in a Temple (Chambry 222)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 222. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Λύκος ἀρνίον ἐδίωκε· τὸ δὲ εἴς τι ἱερὸν κατέφυγε.
sentences.tr: Lykos arnion ediōke· to de eis ti hieron katephyge.
sentences.l: A wolf was pursuing a lamb; and it fled for refuge into a temple.
sentences.n: ἀρνίον is a diminutive of ἀρήν and neuter, so every pronoun for the lamb that follows is neuter. καταφεύγω is the proper word for taking sanctuary, and the right of asylum a temple gave is the hinge of the whole fable.

sentences.t: Προσκαλουμένου δὲ αὐτὸ τοῦ λύκου καὶ λέγοντος ὅτι θυσιάσει αὐτὸ ὁ ἱερεύς, εἰ καταλάβῃ, τῷ θεῷ, ἐκεῖνο ἔφη· « Ἀλλ’ αἱρετώτερόν μοί ἐστι θεοῦ θυσίαν γενέσθαι ἢ ὑπὸ σοῦ διαφθαρῆναι. »
sentences.tr: Proskaloumenou de auto tou lykou kai legontos hoti thysiasei auto ho hiereus, ei katalabēi, tōi theōi, ekeino ephē· « All’ hairetōteron moi esti theou thysian genesthai ē hypo sou diaphtharēnai. »
sentences.l: And the wolf calling it over to himself and saying that the priest would sacrifice it, if he caught it, to the god, that one said: « But it is more to be chosen for me to become a god's sacrifice than to be destroyed by you. »
sentences.i: The wolf called it over to him, saying that if the priest caught it he would sacrifice it to the god; and the lamb said: « But I would rather become a god's sacrifice than be destroyed by you. »
sentences.n: A pair of genitive absolutes, προσκαλουμένου … λέγοντος, sets the wolf's speech as the circumstance and leaves the lamb as the subject of the main verb. προσκαλέομαι is to summon a person to oneself. ὅτι after a verb of saying keeps the tense actually spoken, so θυσιάσει is the wolf's own future. αἱρετώτερον is the comparative of the verbal adjective αἱρετός, 'to be chosen', with ἤ, 'than', after it.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος δηλοῖ ὅτι οἷς ἐπίκειται τὸ ἀποθανεῖν κρείττων ἐστὶν ὁ μετὰ δόξης θάνατος.
sentences.tr: Ho logos dēloi hoti hois epikeitai to apothanein kreittōn estin ho meta doxēs thanatos.
sentences.l: The story shows that for those upon whom dying is laid, the death that comes with honour is the better one.
sentences.i: The story shows that where death cannot be escaped, it is better to die with honour.
sentences.n: ἐπίκειται is 'lies upon', of a fate imposed, with οἷς the dative of those it lies upon. τὸ ἀποθανεῖν is the articular infinitive used as a noun, 'the dying'. δόξα is what others say of you — repute and honour in their eyes, not any inward glory.
